stories.headline: SK hynix approves $38B for two new Korean fabs to chase AI memory demand

key_facts.fact: SK hynix's board approved roughly 54 trillion won (about $38.1 billion) on August 7, 2026 to build new fabs in Yongin and Cheongju.
key_facts.excerpt: The company approved a total investment of approximately 54 trillion, 35.2 trillion won in Yongin "Y2" fab and 19.1 trillion won in the Cheongju "M17" fab, in a board meeting.

key_facts.fact: Yongin Y2 will be a DRAM base of about 1,130,000 m2, breaking ground in July 2027 and opening its first cleanroom in June 2029 to make HBM and next-generation DRAM.
key_facts.excerpt: It will serve as a DRAM production base spanning a total floor area of 341,000 pyeong (approximately 1,130,000m2). Construction is scheduled to break ground in July next year, targeting the opening of its first cleanroom in June 2029 to produce high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and other next-generation DRAM products.

key_facts.fact: Cheongju M17 will be a NAND fab of about 680,000 m2, breaking ground in February 2027 with a first cleanroom in December 2028 and investment running through April 2031.
key_facts.excerpt: Cheongju M17 will be built across a total area of 206,000 pyeong(approximately 680,000m2), breaking ground in February next year with plans to open its first cleanroom in December 2028. The investment period runs through April 2031 according to the master plan.

key_facts.fact: The decision executes a master plan announced in June to spend 600 trillion won on the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster and 100 trillion won on Cheongju; Y1 is already under construction with a cleanroom target of February 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Under its master plan to invest 600 trillion won in the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster and 100 trillion won to expand its Cheongju production base, SK hynix is currently constructing its first fab in Yongin (Y1).

key_facts.fact: Memory prices have surged on short supply and heavy AI demand, with investors watching for shifts in the supply-demand imbalance.
key_facts.excerpt: Memory prices have surged because of short supply and huge demand with investors watching closely for any changes to the supply-demand imbalance.

key_facts.fact: SK hynix has pulled forward completion of the four-fab Yongin cluster by 12 years, from 2045 to 2033.
key_facts.excerpt: The Yongin cluster will eventually house four fabs, including Y1 and Y2, across approximately 4.16 million square meters. SK Hynix has moved up its completion target by 12 years, from 2045 to 2033.

stories.headline: AMD buys Taalas, the startup that etches AI model weights directly into silicon

key_facts.fact: AMD announced on August 6, 2026 a definitive agreement to acquire Taalas, a specialized AI inference silicon company; terms were not disclosed.
key_facts.excerpt: SANTA CLARA, Calif., Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) today announced it has reached a definitive agreement to acquire Taalas, a pioneer in specialized AI inference silicon.

key_facts.fact: Taalas was founded in 2023 in Toronto and its technology optimizes inference dataflows, cutting the compute and memory bottlenecks of general-purpose architectures.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Toronto, Canada, Taalas' technology optimizes inference dataflows, significantly reducing compute and memory bottlenecks associated with general-purpose architectures

key_facts.fact: Instead of storing model weights in HBM, Taalas chips etch them directly into the silicon, making them effectively model-specific integrated circuits.
key_facts.excerpt: The startup's chips don't rely on HBM to store the model weights but rather etch them directly into the silicon. In a sense, Taalas' chips are really model-specific integrated circuits or MSICs.

key_facts.fact: The deal was announced at market close on Thursday and is framed in the same context as Nvidia's $20 billion Groq deal in December: making premium inference for AI agents faster and cheaper.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal, announced at market close on Thursday, appears to be framed in much same context as Nvidia's $20 billion deal with Groq December: make high-performance "premium" inference services prized for AI agents, like code assistants, faster and cheaper to run.

key_facts.fact: Taalas was co-founded by former Tenstorrent CEO Ljubisa Bajic; he and the team will join AMD under Vamsi Boppana's AI organization.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD has acquired Taalas, the AI inference chip startup co-founded by former Tenstorrent CEO Ljubisa Bajic. Bajic, a former AMD executive, and the Taalas team will join AMD under Vamsi Boppana's AI organization.

key_facts.fact: Hardwiring a model means only one model runs per chip; switching models requires new masks, and Taalas aims to tape out workload-specific chips in about two months.
key_facts.excerpt: Inference runs very fast, but almost all the programmability is removed, so only one model can be run. Switching to a new model requires designing a new chip... the company aims to tape-out workload-specific chips in around two months.

key_facts.fact: AMD plans to fold the technology into its accelerator roadmap alongside Instinct GPUs, EPYC CPUs, ROCm and Helios rackscale systems; the deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD says the technology will join its accelerator roadmap, working alongside its Instinct GPUs... The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter.

stories.headline: Unitree prices Shanghai IPO at $9B valuation, with DeepSeek as strategic investor

key_facts.fact: Unitree Robotics priced its STAR Market IPO at 150.80 yuan ($22.3) per share in a filing made public on Thursday, August 6, seeking to raise 6.1 billion yuan.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese robotics company Unitree Robotics has set the price for its initial public offering (IPO) on Shanghai's STAR Market at 150.80 yuan ($22.3) per share, seeking to raise 6.1 billion yuan, according to a filing made public on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: The pricing values the Hangzhou company at roughly 61 billion yuan, or about $9.04 billion, and would make it China's first mainland-listed humanoid robot maker.
key_facts.excerpt: Unitree has priced its Shanghai initial public offering at 150.8 yuan ($22.34) per share, giving the Hangzhou-based robotics company a valuation of roughly 61 billion yuan, or $9.04 billion.

key_facts.fact: The offering covers about 40.44 million shares, or 10% of enlarged share capital, with subscriptions opening August 10 and payment due August 12.
key_facts.excerpt: The IPO subscription starts on August 10, with payment due by August 12. The company plans to issue about 40.44 million shares, representing 10 percent of its enlarged share capital after the offering, according to the filing.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek's parent, Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Basic Technology Research, took 933,400 shares for about 141 million yuan ($20.8 million) in the strategic placement, and the two agreed to jointly develop AI models for humanoid machines.
key_facts.excerpt: The Chinese AI startup invested 140.8 million yuan, or about $20.8 million, in Unitree through the IPO's strategic placement... DeepSeek received 933,399 shares, accounting for 2.31% of shares allocated through the strategic placement. The two companies have agreed to jointly develop AI models for humanoid machines.

key_facts.fact: Nine strategic investors joined the placement, including Tencent, PetroChina, China Southern Power Grid and the National Council for Social Security Fund; strategic subscriptions total about 8.08 million shares, 20% of the offering.
key_facts.excerpt: Unitree Robotics announced the results of its strategic placement on Thursday, showing that nine investors had participated. Among them were Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Basic Technology Research Co, Tencent, PetroChina, and China Southern Power Grid Co

key_facts.fact: Unitree projects first-half 2026 revenue of 1.052 to 1.128 billion yuan and adjusted net profit of 236 to 283 million yuan.
key_facts.excerpt: Unitree Robotics expects its revenue to range between 1.052 billion yuan and 1.128 billion yuan in the first half of 2026. Net profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company, excluding non-recurring gains and losses, is projected to stand between 236 million yuan and 283 million yuan

stories.headline: Firmus raises $2B from Nvidia, Blackstone and Jane Street at over $10.5B valuation

key_facts.fact: Firmus said on Friday, August 7, that it raised $2 billion in equity, lifting its post-money valuation above $10.5 billion, nearly double the $5.5 billion it fetched in April.
key_facts.excerpt: Firmus said on Friday it had raised $2 billion in equity in its latest funding round to speed up the build-out of AI factories in Australia and Asia Pacific, bringing up the company's post-money valuation to above $10.5 billion... nearly double the $5.5 billion valuation from its earlier round in April.

key_facts.fact: The round had follow-on participation from Nvidia and Coatue, plus new money from Blackstone Tactical Opportunities and other Blackstone vehicles and from Jane Street.
key_facts.excerpt: The round includes follow-on participation from Coatue and NVIDIA, alongside new investment from funds managed by Blackstone Tactical Opportunities and other Blackstone vehicles ("Blackstone"), with additional participation from global trading and technology firm Jane Street.

key_facts.fact: The transaction brings Firmus's total new equity raised over the past year to more than $3 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: This transaction brings Firmus' total new equity raised over the past year to more than USD$3 billion, with the post-money valuation now above USD$10.5 billion.

key_facts.fact: Proceeds fund the next phase of Project Southgate, Firmus's AI training and inference build-out in Australia, and expansion into other Asia-Pacific markets including Indonesia.
key_facts.excerpt: The capital will accelerate the rollout of Firmus' Project Southgate AI Factory across Australia and fund early steps toward expansion into other Asia-Pacific markets, including Indonesia.

key_facts.fact: Firmus builds its infrastructure on Nvidia's DSX AI Factory reference architecture and manufactures its own HyperCube platform in Australia.
key_facts.excerpt: With Firmus' Australian manufacturing capability for its proprietary HyperCube platform and grid-aware software already established, the capital enables Firmus to accelerate its Australian rollout... Firmus is building AI infrastructure based on NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Reference Architecture

key_facts.fact: In June, Firmus signed a US$30 billion deal with Nvidia for a 360-megawatt AI factory in Batam, Indonesia, 26 km from Singapore.
key_facts.excerpt: In June, Firmus announced it had signed a US$30bn (A$43bn) deal with Nvidia to build one of Asia-Pacific's biggest AI data centres, a 360-megawatt Nvidia DSX "AI factory, in Batam, Indonesia, just 26km from Singapore.

stories.headline: US Commerce reviews how Chinese AI firms rent Nvidia chips in foreign data centers

key_facts.fact: The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security is reviewing how Chinese AI companies access Nvidia chips overseas, including by legally renting foreign data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: Sources: the US Commerce Department's BIS is reviewing how Chinese AI companies access Nvidia chips overseas, including by legally renting foreign data centers (Mackenzie Hawkins/Bloomberg)

key_facts.fact: Regulators were prompted by fresh technical breakthroughs from Chinese firms suggesting they still use powerful American processors despite export restrictions.
key_facts.excerpt: Regulators' attention was drawn to new technological achievements by Chinese companies, indicating that they continue to use powerful American processors despite Washington's export restrictions.

key_facts.fact: The workaround under scrutiny involves data centers and cloud services in third countries: the chips never physically enter China, but Chinese companies get access to their compute.
key_facts.excerpt: One way to circumvent direct restrictions may be the use of data centers and cloud services in third countries. In this case, the chips do not physically enter China, but Chinese companies gain access to their computing capabilities.

key_facts.fact: No new restriction has been adopted yet; the review could lead to tighter control over data centers and cloud platforms serving Chinese customers.
key_facts.excerpt: The review could serve as grounds for further tightening control over data centers and cloud platforms that provide Chinese customers access to American technologies. At the same time, the adoption of new restrictions has not yet been reported.

key_facts.fact: In May 2026 BIS had already issued guidance that a license is required to export advanced computing items to entities headquartered in China or Macau, or whose ultimate parent is, even when the entity sits outside those places.
key_facts.excerpt: a license is required to export advanced computing items to entities headquartered in Country Group D:5 ... or Macau or with an ultimate parent company headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau - even if the entities themselves are located outside Country Group D:5 or Macau.

key_facts.fact: That May guidance explicitly did not require data center operators to stop using or servicing advanced computing items already in place.
key_facts.excerpt: Bona fide operators of data centers who are otherwise engaged in activities consistent with the EAR are not required to cease the ongoing use, storage, disposal, or servicing of advanced computing items because of this guidance, until further notice from BIS.

stories.headline: Trump sets 15% tariff and minimum import prices on polysilicon, the base of chips and solar

key_facts.fact: On Thursday, August 6, the White House imposed price floors and a 15% tariff on products made from polysilicon, the raw material for semiconductors and solar panels that China mostly produces.
key_facts.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Aug 6 (Reuters) - The White House on Thursday imposed a series of price floors and a 15% tariff on products made from polysilicon, the raw material used in semiconductors and solar panels that is primarily produced by China.

key_facts.fact: The proclamation sets minimum import prices of $21 per kg for polysilicon, $100 per kg for ingots and wafers, $0.22 per watt for solar cells and $0.38 per watt for solar modules.
key_facts.excerpt: (i) $21 per kilogram for polysilicon; (ii) $100 per kilogram for polysilicon ingots and wafers; (iii) $0.22 per watt for solar cells; and (iv) $0.38 per watt for solar modules.

key_facts.fact: Both the minimum import price program and the 15% ad valorem duty take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern time on December 4, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Effective with respect to goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on December 4, 2026, imports of polysilicon ingots and polysilicon derivatives specified in Annexes I and II of this proclamation shall be subject to an additional 15 percent ad valorem rate of duty

key_facts.fact: The action was taken under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 and follows recommendations from Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick after a national security investigation.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump said in the order that he had accepted recommendations by Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick to set minimum import prices as well as a 15% tariff on polysilicon and related imports.

key_facts.fact: The US share of global polysilicon production fell from 50% in 2005 to under 2% in 2024; likely beneficiaries are Hemlock Semiconductor and Wacker Chemie.
key_facts.excerpt: imports have led to the US' share of global polysilicon production to fall from 50% in 2005 to less than 2% in 2024... The order is likely to benefit Hemlock Semiconductor and Wacker Chemie, which are the main producers of the material in the US.

key_facts.fact: The chip industry accounts for just 2.4% of global polysilicon demand, so domestic chipmaking depends on solar demand to sustain production of the material.
key_facts.excerpt: Domestic semiconductor manufacturing depends on solar because the solar industry's larger demand for polysilicon helps support production of the material required for chips. The chip industry accounts for 2.4% of global polysilicon demand, according to the Semiconductor Industry Association.

stories.headline: Singapore's Acrab raises $130M Series B for edge AI chips that run 100B-parameter models locally

key_facts.fact: Acrab announced a $130 million Series B on August 6, 2026, with continued backing from Vertex Ventures SEA & India and Vertex Growth plus institutional investors in Europe and Southeast Asia.
key_facts.excerpt: SINGAPORE, Aug. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Acrab today announced a US$130 million Series B financing round, with continued support from existing leading investors Vertex Ventures SEA & India and Vertex Growth, as well as participation from renowned institutional investors across Europe and Southeast Asia.

key_facts.fact: The round takes Acrab's cumulative funding past $350 million since it was founded in 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: With this round, Acrab's total funding has surpassed $350m since its founding in 2024.

key_facts.fact: Acrab's GELIX 1 is a 5-nanometre edge AI system-on-chip that runs open-source models of up to 100 billion parameters locally instead of in the cloud.
key_facts.excerpt: Last month, Acrab introduced GΞLIX 1, its first-generation edge AI SoC. The chip, built on a 5-nanometre process, supports local deployment of open-source models with up to 100 billion parameters.

key_facts.fact: The chip carries a 20-core Arm CPU, multicore NPU acceleration and unified memory bandwidth, and powers Agent Box, a personal edge AI device that runs inference on-device without continuous cloud access.
key_facts.excerpt: It incorporates a 20-core Arm CPU, multicore NPU acceleration... Agent Box is a personal edge AI device intended for persistent, on-site operation, enabling local inference, multimodal sensing, and agent orchestration without relying on continuous cloud access.

key_facts.fact: Acrab is led by CEO Ken Phua, previously head of Asia applications engineering at Arm and co-CEO of Arm China; Temasek-backed Vertex was among its earliest investors.
key_facts.excerpt: Ken Phua leads Acrab as CEO, following previous roles as head of Asia Applications Engineering at Arm and co-CEO at Arm China. Vertex, a global venture platform backed by Temasek, was among Acrab's earliest investors.

key_facts.fact: The company says it has visible paths to industrial deployments and expects revenue within 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The company said it has visible paths to industrial deployments across multiple domains and expects revenue within 2026.
